description: A floating signal trigger that long-presses open into a staggered line or arc of color-block actions you can slide across and release to fire; the trigger confirms with a check, tap toggles, a scrim dismisses, and the glass morphs on iOS 26.

contents.content: Floating action menu with a hold-slide-release gesture, staggered emergence, a dimming scrim and a confirming trigger.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Two ways in: a tap toggles the menu, a 350ms hold expands it and keeps the same touch live, so you can slide across items (each crossing lifts the item and ticks `.selection`) and release to fire. Releasing a hold on empty space leaves the menu open.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Items emerge one at a time (45ms stagger, reversed on collapse) and labels fade in only after the last item has landed. On iOS 26 each item carries a `glassEffectID` inside a `GlassEffectContainer`, so the glass blends with the trigger as it travels; earlier the same choreography runs on `.regularMaterial`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The scrim is an oversized background behind the trigger; it dims everything beneath the menu in its parent and dismisses on tap. Place the menu last in a `ZStack` so nothing sits above it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Phases: `collapsed`, `expanding`, `open`, `hovering`, `firing`, `collapsing`. Reduce Motion drops the stagger and the lift and crossfades instead; Reduce Transparency swaps glass and Material for opaque fills.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver sees the trigger as a button (double tap toggles) and each item as its own button while the menu is open.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The trigger defaults to the house signal color with dark ink (`tint` is now optional; `nil` uses `Style.trigger`). After an action fires it shows a checkmark for 0.9s (`Style.confirmsAction`).

title: Glass Segments
description: A segmented control whose glass indicator you can grab and drag: it lifts under the finger, rubber-bands past the ends, stretches with velocity and settles with a spring, while the label ink flips exactly under its edge; tap still works.

contents.content: Visual tuning for `GlassSegments`. `standard` is a solid track with a glass indicator; set `indicatorTint` for a color block indicator.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A touch that lands on the indicator grabs it: it lifts (scale 1.04, deeper shadow), follows the finger, rubber-bands up to one segment past either end and stretches along the drag with velocity. Release commits to the segment the flick would land on (`predictedEndLocation`) with a `.spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.3)`. A touch anywhere else is a plain tap on that segment.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One `.selection` haptic fires each time the indicator's center crosses into a new segment, and once on tap; there is no second tick on release.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Label emphasis is continuous: each label's opacity tracks how much of the indicator overlaps it, so the emphasis hands over during the drag instead of swapping at the end.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Transparency swaps the track for an opaque system fill. Reduce Motion removes the stretch and the lift scale and shortens the settle.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Segments share the width equally; the control fills its container, so constrain it with `.frame(width:)` when you want it compact.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Labels are drawn twice: once in `Style.ink`, and once in `Style.selectedInk` masked to the indicator's live shape, so the color hands over exactly under the indicator edge while dragging or stretching.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The indicator is a solid fill (`indicatorSurface`, or `indicatorTint` for a color block) under clear Liquid Glass on iOS 26, so it reads on the track in light and dark. `GlassSegmentsStyle.block(_:)` makes a block indicator with dark ink.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`GlassSegments.Style`, alias of `GlassSegmentsStyle`): `track`, `ink`, `selectedInk`, `indicatorTint`, `indicatorSurface`, `font`, `disabledOpacity`. `.disabled(true)` fades the control and ignores touches. The row height scales with Dynamic Type (capped at 1.5x).

title: Glass Surface
description: The Glass family foundation: Liquid Glass in a capsule, rect, circle or concentric shape on iOS 26, with a layered Material fallback that keeps the press response, solid tint, specular edge and a designed disabled state everywhere else.

contents.content: Liquid Glass on iOS 26, a layered Material surface everywhere else, with the same press feel on both.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On iOS 26 this is real `.glassEffect(_:in:)`; earlier, or under Reduce Transparency, it is `.regularMaterial` (opaque `secondarySystemBackground` under Reduce Transparency) with a top light, a two-layer soft shadow and a specular edge: a bright top highlight plus a faint `.primary` edge.

The press is tracked with a simultaneous gesture, so a `Button` inside still owns the tap. Reduce Motion drops the scale but keeps the brighten and haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.concentric(minimum:)` resolves to `ConcentricRectangle` on iOS 26 (set `.containerShape` on the parent) and to a continuous rounded rect with `minimum` as the radius earlier.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `GlassSurface.Group(spacing:)` is `GlassEffectContainer` on iOS 26 so neighbouring surfaces blend where they meet; earlier it is a transparent wrapper.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`.standard`): `tintAmount` (0.72, so a tinted fallback reads as a color block), `specular`, `shadow`, `pressedScale` (0.96), `disabledOpacity` and `solidFill` for Reduce Transparency.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Disabled: `.disabled(true)` fades and desaturates the surface and silences the press response on both paths.

title: Address Field
description: An address field for checkout, delivery and sign-up that lists type-ahead suggestions under a soft 56pt block with the matched text in bold, picks one with a tap or the hardware keyboard, shows a spinner on the chosen row while it resolves into a structured address with street, city, state, postal code, country and coordinate, then settles into the field with the locality on a second line and a sage check, keeping the typed text usable with a "Use as typed" row and an inline retry when a lookup fails.

contents.content: Address entry with type-ahead suggestions that resolve to a structured, verified address. Typing searches after a short pause (three characters or more). Each new keystroke cancels the search in flight, so a slow answer for an older query never replaces a newer one. Picking a suggestion looks up the full address; when it arrives, `address` is set, `text` becomes the address's first line (usually the street) and the locality shows under it. Editing the text again clears `address`. Location permission is never requested: suggestions come from the query alone, optionally biased by `region`. `swift @State private var query = "" @State private var address: AddressField.Address? AddressField("Delivery address", text: $query, address: $address, countries: ["US", "CA"]) `

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Typing searches once the trimmed text is three characters or more, after a 250ms pause. The search runs in a task keyed on the text, so every keystroke cancels the one in flight: a slow answer for an older query can never replace a newer list. Earlier suggestions stay on screen while the next ones load, with a small spinner in the field instead of a flicker.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Suggestions come from `MKLocalSearchCompleter` with `resultTypes = .address`, at most five, the matched runs in bold and the locality on a second line. Picking one runs an `MKLocalSearch` for that completion, with a spinner on the chosen row and the other rows dimmed. Picking another row, editing the text or leaving the screen cancels the lookup, and a late answer is ignored.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Once resolved, `address` holds the street, city, state, postal code, country, ISO country code, coordinate and a single line formatted for the address's own country. `text` becomes the first line (usually the street), the rest shows under it in the field and a sage check appears. `mailingLines` gives the label lines in the country's postal order.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Editing the text clears `address`. Setting `address` from outside (a saved address) fills the field without searching; setting `text` and `address` together is not treated as an edit.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A failed lookup stays on its row in red with a Retry pill; a failed suggestion request shows "Couldn't load suggestions" with Retry. No matches is a quiet line. In each of these cases a "Use as typed" row sets an address with `isVerified == false` holding only the typed text. Turn it off with `allowsUnverified: false`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `countries: ["US", "CA"]` leaves out suggestions whose last line names another country, and a picked address outside the list shows "Choose an address in United States" on its row instead of being set. `region` biases suggestions toward an area. Location permission is never requested.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: iOS 26 moves map items to `MKAddress`, which has no separate street or postal code, and deprecates `MKPlacemark`. On iOS 17 to 25 the parts come from the placemark; on iOS 26 from the item's placemark read dynamically (so the file builds without deprecation warnings), with `MKAddressRepresentations` for the formatted line, city and country as the fallback.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `source:` swaps MapKit for your own backend, or a fixed list for previews and tests. Both calls are cancelled when their result is no longer wanted.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hardware keyboard: up and down arrows move the highlight, Return picks the highlighted row (or the top one), Escape closes the list. A long street wraps up to three lines. A pasted multi-line address is joined with commas.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The list sits inline under the field and pushes content down, so it scrolls with a form and never clips inside a scroll view. Leaving the field hides it; coming back shows it again.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the field's hint says whether the address is verified; the suggestion count ("5 suggestions", inflected), "Finding address", the result and any error are announced; rows are buttons read as title and locality with the selected trait when highlighted.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a soft impact on pick, success when the address resolves, error when a lookup fails, selection ticks for arrow-key moves. Nothing per keystroke.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: rows and the field grow and wrap; at accessibility sizes the leading glyphs step aside so titles get the width.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the field, label, secondary label, focus ring, row highlight, success, error and ink colors, the corner radius and the minimum height.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the list, check and rows fade instead of sliding and scaling.

title: Amount Field
description: A currency amount entry that formats live in the user's locale as each digit lands (grouping, decimal separator, symbol before or after, the currency's own fraction digits), with a large auto-fitting figure whose digits roll in, a blinking caret right after the digits, robust paste of amounts like "$1,234.56" or "1 234,56 €", and a limit that refuses the keystroke with a damped shake, an error haptic and a message line, all backed by a `Decimal` binding.

contents.content: Currency amount entry with live locale formatting, a `Decimal` value and a limit. The field keeps its own digit buffer and renders the formatted string itself, so the caret never jumps and locale separators never break parsing. Formatting follows `\.locale`; fraction digits come from the currency.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The field keeps its own buffer of typed digits and renders the formatted string itself. A hidden `TextField` with `.decimalPad` captures keys, so the caret never jumps and grouping separators never reach a parser. The caret is drawn right after the digits, before a trailing symbol ("1.234,56| €").

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The value is a `Decimal`. Fraction digits come from the currency through `Decimal.FormatStyle.Currency`: JPY takes none, USD two, KWD three. Formatting follows `\.locale`, so `.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: "de_DE"))` gives "1.234,56 €", en\_IN groups in lakhs ("₹1,23,456") and ar\_SA shows Arabic-Indic digits.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: While typing, what you typed is what you see: "12." keeps its separator and "12.50" keeps its zero. Leading zeros are stripped, "." on an empty field starts "0.", a second separator is ignored and digits past the currency's precision are dropped. Leaving the field settles "12.5" to "12.50" and "12." to "12".

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Both "." and "," (and the Arabic decimal separator) work as the decimal key, whatever the device region. Digits in any script are accepted and stored as ASCII.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Paste (long-press, or Command-V) parses "1,234.56", "$99", "1 234,56 €", "US$ 12" and Arabic-Indic text. A lone separator followed by exactly three digits reads as thousands unless the currency has three decimals. Words, two numbers or a minus sign are rejected with an error haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `limit` refuses the keystroke or paste that would pass it: a damped shake, an `.error` haptic, a VoiceOver announcement and the `limitMessage` line, which fades after a moment. An external value over the limit is shown in `Style.error` with the message, not clamped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: External writes to the binding (a quick-amount chip, a reset) redraw the display at the currency's precision. Negative or over-precise values are normalized and written back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.hero` is a large light figure that scales down to fit its width, with digits rolling in through `.numericText()`. `.compact` is a 56pt block with a focus ring. Both follow Dynamic Type.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver reads the label and the full formatted amount as the value ("$1,234.56"), and the limit as a hint. `.disabled(true)` dims the field and blocks focus. `isFocused` lets you raise or dismiss the keyboard.

contents.heading: notes

title: Date Range Picker
description: A start-to-end date range picker on a paged month grid built from the environment calendar and locale, where the first tap drops a solid butter start block, the second closes the range and a soft band sweeps day by day between the two blocks, wrapping across week rows with rounded caps, while sold-out days are struck through, a maximum length dims unreachable days, months page by swipe or chevrons with a rolling title, and a summary reads out the dates and nights.

contents.content: Day-granular start/end range picker with a paged month grid. The selection is always two start-of-day dates in the environment `Calendar` and `TimeZone` (`upperBound` is the start of the last day, e.g. the check-out day for a stay). The first tap sets a start, the second closes the range (a day before the start becomes the new start), and a third tap starts over. A range can never contain a disabled or out-of-bounds day: an end tap that would span one, or that exceeds `maximumLength`, is refused with an error haptic and a short notice, and the start stays in place.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The selection is a `ClosedRange<Date>` of start-of-day dates in the environment `Calendar` and `TimeZone`. `upperBound` is the start of the last day (the check-out day for a stay). Dates you pass in are normalized to their day.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: First tap sets the start and clears any old range, second tap sets the end, third tap starts a new range. Tapping a day before the pending start moves the start there. In `.nights` mode tapping the start again cancels it; in `.days` mode it confirms a one-day range.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A range never contains an unavailable day. An end tap that would span a day marked by `isDateDisabled` or outside `bounds`, or that exceeds `maximumLength`, is refused: the start stays, an `.error` haptic plays, and a notice chip ("Includes unavailable dates", "Up to 14 nights") replaces the length chip for two seconds. While a start is pending, days that cannot close the range are dimmed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The grid comes from the calendar: `firstWeekday`, days per week, days in the month and the weekday offset all come from `Calendar` APIs, so Hebrew, Islamic, Ethiopic and other calendars lay out correctly. Weekday symbols are the calendar's very short standalone symbols; day numbers, month titles and the summary use `Date.FormatStyle` and `Date.IntervalFormatStyle` in the environment locale, including native digits.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Day math uses `Calendar.date(byAdding:)` and counts days on civil dates, never 86,400 second steps, so 23 and 25 hour DST days and time zones whose midnight is skipped stay exact.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The band is drawn per cell as half-cell pieces under the endpoint blocks, so it reads as one strip that wraps across week rows with rounded caps at row edges and at month edges. When a range completes it sweeps in from the start, one day at a time. `UnevenRoundedRectangle` uses leading and trailing radii, so caps mirror in right-to-left layouts, where the grid also flows right to left.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Months page with the chevrons or a horizontal swipe (a paging `ScrollView`), and the title rolls in the paging direction. Paging stops at the months of `bounds`; without bounds it spans five years either side of today and the selection's month.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The summary shows the range in the locale's interval pattern ("Mar 4 – 9") and a length chip in `counting` units, pluralized with automatic grammar agreement.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: `.selection` when a start is set, `.success` when a range completes, `.error` on a refused end.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: each day is a button labeled with its full date ("Tuesday, March 4", plus the year outside the current one, and "Today" first for today), with the `.isSelected` trait inside the range and a value of Start date, End date, In range or Unavailable. Month changes, completed ranges and refusals are announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: day cells grow with `@ScaledMetric` from 44pt up to 76pt tall; day numbers scale to accessibility sizes and shrink to fit rather than clip. The summary stacks when it no longer fits on one line.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: no sweep, springs or rolling title. The swipe no longer slides the grid; both the swipe and the chevrons crossfade to the next month.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the ground, day text, muted text, band, endpoint blocks, ink on blocks, the today dot, disabled days, the month buttons, the notice chip and the corner radius. `.disabled(true)` dims the picker and stops taps and paging.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For booking a time slot inside a day, see the slot picker in SwiftPieces Pro.

title: Expanding Track
description: A thumbless slider drawn as a solid color bar that swells from 8pt to a 32pt block under the finger, shows detent dots and an inverting readout while dragging, squishes past either end, and can carry an uppercase label with a big light numeral; a second init selects a range with two sinking handles.

contents.content: Thumbless slider that swells into a solid block on touch. Bind a `Double` for a single value or a `ClosedRange<Double>` for a range.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: There is no thumb: the whole 44pt row is the hit area and the value follows the finger's x position directly, so the bar can rest at 8pt and still be easy to grab. While dragging it swells to a 32pt block (`Style.activeHeight`) with detent dots at each `step` and a soft shadow.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pass `title` for the labeled layout: an uppercase caption with the value as a big light numeral above the track, decimals dimmed at the locale's separator. Without a title the value prints inside the block while dragging, drawn twice so it switches to `ink` where the fill passes under it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dragging past either end squishes the track toward the far edge with a rubber-band curve (asymptote 22pt) and fires a rigid impact once when the value hits the bound; release springs it back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Selection ticks fire per `step` crossing, or every tenth of the span when there is no step; the optional symbol plays `.variableColor` only when the value rises past a tick.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The range init keeps the handles apart by `minimumDistance` and lets the active ink handle sink into the block; VoiceOver gets separate "Minimum" and "Maximum" adjustable elements, prefixed with the title when there is one.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` carries the trough, the fill block, ink, labels and track metrics. `.standard` is the house palette (tangerine on a quiet trough); pass `.init(fill:)` to use another block. `.disabled(true)` greys the fill.

contents.heading: notes

title: Form Field
description: A text field on a soft 56pt block whose label rests inside as a placeholder and glides up into a caption on focus or once filled, with an optional leading icon, a clear button, help text, a grapheme-accurate character limit with a counter that turns into a tangerine chip and bumps when extra input is refused, and validation that waits until you leave the field before drawing an error ring, sliding in the message with an error haptic and a VoiceOver announcement, then shows a sage check once fixed.

contents.content: Text field with a floating label, help and error text, a character limit and a counter. Chain fields by applying `.focused($focus, equals: .email)` to each `FormField` (focus reaches the text field inside) and moving focus in `onSubmit`. Apply `SwiftUI/View/formFieldRevealsErrors(_:)` to a form to show every field's validation at once, for example after a submit button is tapped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The label is one `Text` in `.body` that moves between two alignments and scales down into a reserved caption slot. The scale is the caption-to-body line-height ratio at the current Dynamic Type size, so the label lands in the same place at every size, including the accessibility sizes, with no font swap and no jump.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `prompt` shows only while the field is focused and empty, under the floated label. The system placeholder is suppressed so the label is never drawn twice.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `limit` counts extended grapheme clusters (`String.count`), so a flag, a family emoji or a letter with a combining accent is one character. Typing or pasting past the limit trims with `prefix(limit)`, which never cuts a character in half. A refused keystroke fires a light impact and bumps the counter. At the limit the counter becomes a solid `Style.error` chip with ink text.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The counter is `count/limit` with localized digits. With an IME that composes text (Japanese, Chinese), trimming can end a composition early when it runs past the limit.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Validation timing: `.onBlur` (default) waits until the field has been edited and left, `.onSubmit` waits for Return, `.live` starts with the first edit. After that the field validates on every keystroke, so the error clears the moment the text is fixed and a sage check appears. An `error` passed from outside shows immediately and takes priority.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `formFieldRevealsErrors(true)` on a container arms every field inside, for a Save button that should flag untouched required fields.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: When an error first appears the ring turns `Style.error`, the message slides in under the field with an exclamation glyph, and an `.error` haptic plays once. Help text returns when the error clears.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Focus: apply `.focused($focus, equals: .email)` to the `FormField` itself and move focus in `onSubmit`, with `submitLabel: .next`. Tapping anywhere on the block, including the icon and padding, focuses the field. The clear button appears while focused and non-empty and keeps the keyboard up.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `axis: .vertical` grows up to eight lines. Return inserts a newline there, so `onSubmit` does not fire; put a multiline field last in a chain.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.emailAddress` and `.URL` keyboards (and email, URL and username content types) turn off autocapitalization and autocorrection.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver reads the label, the text with the counter ("12 of 160 characters") as the value, and the error or help as the hint. A new or changed error is announced. The floating label, icon, check and footer are hidden to avoid double reading.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the field, label, secondary, focus ring, error, success and ink colors plus minimum height (44pt floor) and corner radius. `.disabled(true)` dims the field and hides the clear button.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the label still moves (it is the state change) but on a short ease with no bounce, messages crossfade instead of sliding, and the counter changes color without the bump.

title: Location Picker
description: A map picker for delivery, rides, events and listings: drag the map under a fixed red pin that lifts while the map moves and drops with a small bounce when it settles, the address under it is looked up after a short pause with stale answers cancelled and recent ones cached, a floating card shows the street and locality (a dropped pin with coordinates where there is no address, Retry when the lookup fails), the locate button asks for location only when tapped and flies to you, and Confirm hands back the coordinate with its address.

contents.content: A map you drag under a fixed pin to choose an exact spot, with the address of wherever the pin lands. The pin stays in the middle of the visible map. While the map moves it lifts and its shadow spreads; when the map settles it drops with a small bounce, `selection` is set to the coordinate, and the address is looked up after a short pause. A newer settle cancels the lookup in flight, so an address never lands on the wrong spot, and recent answers are cached by position (about 5 m), so nudging back costs no request. Location permission is only requested when the locate button is tapped. `swift @State private var place: LocationPicker.Place? LocationPicker(selection: $place, initialCenter: store.coordinate) { place in order.dropOff = place } `

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The picker takes the size it is given, at least 320 pt tall: full screen, in a sheet, or `.frame(height: 340).clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 26))` inside a form. Bind `selection`, and pass `onConfirm` for the Confirm button. Add `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` to your Info.plist for the locate button. Full screen, the map already runs under the status bar and the home indicator while the card and the locate button stay clear of them, so leave out `.ignoresSafeArea()`, which would push both under the system bars.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The pin stays in the middle of the map the card leaves visible. While the map moves it lifts 12 pt, its shadow spreads and a small mark stays on the exact spot; when the map settles it drops with a small bounce and a light tap. Only a real change of the spot under the pin lifts it, so the camera reports MapKit sends on appear, on rotation and on resize do nothing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `selection` is set when the pin settles (coordinate only) and again when the address arrives. Its coordinate is always where the pin points; the address is the nearest one found. Setting `selection` from outside, a search result or a saved place, moves the map there, and a place that already has an address is shown without a lookup.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The address is looked up 300 ms after the map settles. A new settle, or leaving the screen, cancels the lookup in flight and its request, and an answer for a spot that is no longer under the pin is dropped. Answers are cached per picker by position rounded to about 5 m (the 40 most recent), so nudging back to a known spot sends nothing, which also keeps clear of the geocoder's rate limit.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: iOS 26 uses `MKReverseGeocodingRequest`, reading the street and postal code from the map item's placemark (dynamically, as Address Field does) with `MKAddressRepresentations` as the fallback. iOS 17 to 25 uses `CLGeocoder`, kept in a deprecated function that only runs below iOS 26, so the file builds without warnings on both.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The card has one state per moment: the last address dimmed with "Locating…" while the map moves, loading lines while the address is on its way, street and locality once found, "Dropped pin" with the coordinates where there is no address (open water), and "Couldn't find the address" with the coordinates and Retry when the lookup fails (offline, throttled). Every state keeps the same two lines, and the map's center only moves when the card grows, so nothing jumps as the text changes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Confirm is a red capsule. While the map moves its label dims and it is disabled. Tapped while the address is on its way, it spins and waits for it (up to four seconds), then hands over the place; after a failed lookup it hands over the coordinate alone. Return confirms with a hardware keyboard. Leave out `onConfirm` to hide it and read `selection` yourself.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The locate button asks for When In Use permission on its first tap, never on appear. It spins while finding you, flies the camera to you, and fills in once the pin sits on you; a fix from the last minute is used at once. With approximate location the map shows the area the fix covers instead of a street. When access is denied the arrow is slashed and a tap explains and offers Settings; when it is restricted a tap explains. Dragging works the same without permission.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Where the map starts: the place in `selection`, else `initialCenter`, else the person's location when the app already has permission, else central Lisbon.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: MapKit's logo and legal notice stay visible above the card: the card insets the map's safe area, which is also where MapKit puts the camera's center.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the address readout is one element, "Selected location", with the address, "Dropped pin" and the coordinates, "Locating" or "Finding the address" as its value. Its actions move the map a quarter of the visible span north, south, east or west, zoom in and out, use your location and retry. After the map settles from a move the new address is announced. The pin is decorative and hidden; the locate button reads its state.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a light tap when the pin drops, success when Confirm hands over the place, a selection tick on Retry, and an error when Retry or locating fails. Nothing while panning, and nothing for a lookup that fails on its own.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: the card's text grows and wraps up to accessibility sizes, Retry moves under the text, Confirm stays full width, and the locate button grows up to 64 pt. Right to left, the card mirrors and the locate button sits top left; the map is never mirrored.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the pin dims instead of lifting, the camera jumps instead of flying, the loading lines hold still, and buttons dim instead of dipping when pressed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The map pans and zooms but doesn't rotate or tilt, so north stays up. A drag that starts on the map pans it, inside a `ScrollView` or a `Form` too; in a sheet, the grabber still dismisses.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the card surface, label, secondary label, field, the pin and its ink, Confirm and its ink, the card's corner radius, points of interest (off by default, so the streets and the pin read first) and the muted map (on by default). `Messages` replaces any line, for example `confirm: "Deliver here"`. `Geocoder` swaps MapKit for your own backend, or a fixed answer for previews and tests.

title: Range Slider
description: A dual-thumb slider for a range of values, with two round thumbs on a quiet track and the selected span drawn as a solid color block between them; drag either thumb or touch the track to pull the nearest one over, values snap to a step without floating drift, the thumbs never cross and keep a minimum gap, a grabbed thumb grows and its readout chip fills with the block color, the two readouts merge into one chip instead of colliding, and every step ticks a selection haptic with a firmer impact at a bound or the gap.

contents.content: Dual-thumb slider that binds a `ClosedRange` of any floating-point type. The simplest call is one line: `RangeSlider(value: $price, in: 0...1000, step: 10, format: .currency(code: "USD").precision(.fractionLength(0)))`. Pass a `FormatStyle` or a `(V) -> String` closure as `format`; it drives the readouts and the VoiceOver values.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Generic over any `BinaryFloatingPoint` (`Double`, `Float`, `CGFloat`). Bind a `ClosedRange`; pass `format:` as a `FormatStyle` (`.currency(code: "USD").precision(.fractionLength(0))`, `.percent`) or a `(V) -> String` closure. The format drives the readouts and the VoiceOver values.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Drag either thumb, or touch the track and the nearest thumb glides to the finger. Grabbing a thumb keeps the finger's offset, so it never jumps under the touch. When both thumbs sit on the same point, the first clear movement decides: right (in left-to-right) takes the upper thumb, left takes the lower.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The thumbs never cross. They stop `minimumDistance` apart, kept on the step grid (a 5 gap with step 10 stops at 10).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `step` snaps from `bounds.lowerBound`. Both bounds stay reachable when the span is not a multiple of the step (0...1000 by 30 reaches 1000). Values are rounded to the step's decimal places, so `0.1` steps write `0.3`, not `0.30000000000000004`. Out-of-bounds or reversed bindings are shown clamped and written back clean on the first change.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Readouts: `.thumbs` (default) floats a chip over each thumb, clamped inside the track; when the two would come within 6pt they crossfade into one "lower – upper" chip. A grabbed thumb grows and its chip fills with the block color. `.header` prints "lower – upper" above the track and stacks the values at large text sizes. `.hidden` shows nothing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: `.selection` on each value change while dragging (every 5% of the span without a step), throttled to about 30 per second; a rigid `.impact` once when a thumb reaches a bound or the minimum gap.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Right-to-left: the track mirrors, so the lower thumb sits on the right, and the merged chip reads in the reader's direction.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: two adjustable elements, "Minimum" then "Maximum" (set `lowerLabel` and `upperLabel`, e.g. "Minimum price"). Swipe up or down moves one `step` to the next valid value, or 1% of the span without a step.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Thumbs keep a 44pt touch and VoiceOver target even when `Style.thumbSize` draws them smaller. Readouts use text styles and grow with Dynamic Type.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the track, the fill block, thumb face and border, ink, labels, chips, track height and thumb size. `.disabled(true)` desaturates, dims and blocks input.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: no spring, no thumb growth (the border still thickens), and the thumbs follow the finger without smoothing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The drag starts on touch-down so the track responds to taps; inside a vertical `ScrollView` or sheet, a drag that begins on the slider moves the slider rather than scrolling.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a full filter sheet built around it, see the filter sheet in SwiftPieces Pro.

contents.content: Minus/plus stepper with hold-to-repeat and a horizontal scrub gesture.

contents.content: One `DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)` covers the whole capsule and decides by start location: the round buttons at each end press, the numeral block in the middle starts a scrub. title: Signature Pad
description: A signature field that lays smooth, velocity-weighted ink into a Canvas as the finger moves, thinning on quick flicks and pooling on slow turns, over a baseline whose Sign here hint fades on the first stroke, with Undo, Clear and Undo after Clear, a Type instead mode that sets the typed name in a script face on the same line, strokes that rescale with the pad on rotation, and export to a transparent PNG or a vector PDF.

contents.content: Signature capture that feels like ink, bound to a `SignaturePad.Signature` value you own. Strokes are smoothed through midpoint quadratics and weighted by speed (fast strokes run thin, slow turns run full), drawn in a `Canvas` one layer per stroke so finished strokes never redraw while you sign. Points are stored in the pad's coordinate space together with the pad size they were captured at, so the signature rescales with the pad on rotation and exports at any size. A drag that starts in the pad draws and never scrolls an enclosing `ScrollView`; a drag that starts outside still scrolls. `swift @State private var signature = SignaturePad.Signature() SignaturePad(signature: $signature) Button("Confirm delivery") { upload(signature.pngData(size: CGSize(width: 600, height: 200))) } .disabled(signature.isEmpty) `

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Ink is weighted by speed, the way a pen behaves: each sample's width falls from `Style.lineWidth` toward about 40% of it as the finger speeds up, eased over 35 ms so strokes swell and thin smoothly. The line runs through the midpoints of the touch samples as quadratic curves, cut into short pieces whose widths interpolate, so there are no corners or width steps, and long gaps from very fast strokes are bridged by the same curves.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Each stroke is its own `Canvas` layer, grouped into a few paths by width. Finished strokes never redraw while you sign, so long signatures stay smooth.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A tap draws a dot. `isEmpty` stays `true` until there is at least `Signature.minimumInk` of ink (12% of the pad width, about 40pt on a phone) or a typed name, so a stray tap or speck never enables your submit button. `strokes.isEmpty` tells you whether anything is on the pad at all, and `inkLength` lets you set a stricter rule.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Points are stored in the pad's coordinates together with the pad size they were captured at (`canvasSize`). When the pad changes size (rotation, split view, a different `Style.height`) the signature scales uniformly, anchored to the bottom and the leading edge so it stays on the line next to the cross. Strokes added after a resize join the same space.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Undo removes the last stroke with a short fade and a rigid tick. Clear fades out the whole signature with a medium tick, and Undo right after Clear brings it all back until anything else changes. A soft tick marks the first touch of each stroke. With a hardware keyboard, Command-Z undoes and Command-Delete clears.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The "Sign here" hint fades and drops a few points on the first touch. Reduce Motion keeps the fade and drops the movement.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A drag that starts in the pad draws from the first touch and never scrolls an enclosing `ScrollView` or `Form`; a drag that starts outside the pad scrolls as usual. If the system cancels a touch (a call, a presented sheet), the stroke so far is kept.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Type instead turns the line into a text field set in a script face (Snell Roundhand, a system font, so nothing is bundled). The name sits on the same baseline and shrinks to fit when it is long. Scripts the face lacks fall back to the system font. Drawn strokes are kept while typing, so Draw instead brings them back; while `typedName` is non-nil it is the signature for `isEmpty` and export.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Export: `image(size:scale:ink:lineWidth:trimmed:)` and `pngData` give a transparent PNG, and `pdfData` gives a one-page vector PDF. `trimmed` (the default) crops to the ink so the signature fills the image; `false` keeps the whole pad area with the signature where it sat. Ink defaults to black, whatever the on-screen appearance. A typed signature exports in the same script face. Both can be called off the main actor.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Signature` is `Codable` and `Equatable`, so a draft can be saved and restored, and `.onChange(of:)` sees every stroke.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the pad reads "Signature" with a value of Empty, Too short to count as a signature, or Signed. Double-tapping lets a VoiceOver user draw directly on it (direct touch), and the pad offers Type your name instead, Undo and Clear as actions. Undo, Clear and restores are announced. The typed field reads "Signature, typed name".

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: the controls under the pad scale and stack when they no longer fit on one line. The hint grows up to accessibility sizes and shrinks to fit under the line; the cross and baseline keep a fixed position so they stay aligned with stored strokes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `allowsTyping: false` removes Type instead. It is the accessible path for people who cannot draw a signature, so turn it off only when your flow offers another way to sign.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the pad, ink, label and secondary colors, ink weight, corner radius and pad height (`nil` fills the height offered, for a full-screen signing sheet). `.disabled(true)` dims the pad and stops drawing.

Setting it from outside redraws the pad; a stroke removed from outside inside `withAnimation` fades out.

title: Token Field
description: A tag and recipient field where committed entries become solid color chips with dark ink that wrap across lines while the text field takes the rest of the last line, return, comma or a paste of a whole list commits trimmed tokens with duplicate, limit and validation checks, backspace on an empty field highlights the last chip and a second press removes it, and an inline suggestion list filters as you type.

contents.content: Wrapping token entry bound to an array of strings: tags, skills, recipients.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Chips and the input sit in a private wrapping `Layout`: leading-aligned rows, spacing that scales with Dynamic Type, and the input taking the rest of the last line. When that is narrower than the input's minimum (88pt, scaled) or its typed text, the input wraps to a new full-width line. A chip wider than the field truncates in the middle.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Return, comma (including the full-width `，` and `、`) and pasted line breaks commit the trimmed text by default. `separators` adds `.semicolon` and `.space` for recipient lists. Pasting `a, b, c` adds three tokens in one animated change.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every entry is checked in order: `maxTokens`, then duplicates (case-insensitive, the first spelling is kept and the existing chip is highlighted), then `validate`. Rejected entries stay in the input so they can be fixed, with a damped shake, an error ring and an `.error` haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Backspace on an empty input highlights the last chip with a soft impact; a second backspace removes it with a rigid impact. Tapping a chip highlights it the same way. A zero-width space kept in front of the typed text makes this reliable on the software keyboard, where iOS reports no key event for backspace on an empty field. It is never shown or committed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The input uses a vertical-axis `TextField`, so return inserts a line break the field turns into a commit and the keyboard stays up between tokens. Valid text left in the input is committed quietly when the field loses focus.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Suggestions appear under the field while typing, matched case- and diacritic-insensitively, prefix matches first, at most five, with the matched run in bold and a dot in the color the chip will take. Tokens already added are left out.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Each token keeps the same chip color wherever it appears, picked from its text, so removing one never recolors the rest. Pass a single color in `Style.chips` for uniform chips.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: At `maxTokens` the input stops accepting text and shows a quiet count such as `5/5`. Backspace still removes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tapping anywhere in the field that is not a chip focuses the input. Keyboard type, capitalization and content type pass through: apply `.keyboardType(.emailAddress)` and friends to the `TokenField`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: each chip is one element read as "Swift, token" with a Remove action; the input's label carries the placeholder and the token count; adds, removals and rejections are announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the field, chip colors, ink, label, placeholder, error, corner radius and minimum height. `.disabled(true)` dims the field and disables removal.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: no shake or scale; chips and the suggestion list fade.

title: Depth Carousel
description: Paged cards that recede in depth as they leave center and hand each page a phase value for inner parallax. Neighbors come forward on tap, and a page counter sits beside a scrubbable pill indicator computed in absolute page coordinates so it never jumps.

contents.content: Centered paging carousel with depth recession, per-page parallax phase, and a progress-linked indicator.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Snapping uses `.scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)` with content margins sized so the aligned page is centered; the first and last pages center too. Fractional progress is read from the page row's position in the `.scrollView` coordinate space, so it works on iOS 17 without `onScrollGeometryChange`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Depth is driven by the same progress: pages shrink by `style.recede`, fade by `style.dim`, and their shadow gets lighter and leans back toward the centered page as they leave center. The `phase` handed to your content is -1...1, for inner parallax; the example drifts a cropped ink disc by `phase * 40` inside a solid color card. Under Reduce Motion the phase is 0 and only the dim remains.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tap a neighbor page to bring it to center; the centered page keeps its own gestures.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Under the pages, a "01 / 04" counter (current page in rounded semibold, total dimmed, rolling as it changes) sits at the page's leading edge, and the pill track sits at its trailing edge. The pill is positioned in absolute page coordinates, so it tracks the finger and never jumps when a page settles; it widens while dragging. The whole 44pt-tall track is scrubbable, with a selection haptic per page.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`DepthCarousel.Style`, also `DepthCarouselStyle`): `recede`, `dim`, `shadowOpacity`, `indicatorActive`, `indicatorInactive`, `showsCounter`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver treats the carousel as one container that reads "Page x of y" and supports swipe up/down to change pages; the indicator is hidden from it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `scrollClipDisabled()` lets neighbor pages peek past the carousel's own bounds, so give it full width.

title: Drag Select Grid
description: A multi-select photo and file grid where one drag paints a whole reading-order range the way the system photo library does, a sideways drag or a short hold starts painting while vertical swipes still scroll, dragging back unpaints, starting on a selected item deselects, the grid auto-scrolls faster the deeper the finger sits in the top or bottom edge, and selected cells inset under a check badge with a haptic tick per item.

contents.content: A scrolling grid of `Identifiable` items with drag-to-select: photos, files, attachments, media. In selection mode a sideways drag (or a short hold, then any direction) paints every item from the first one touched to the one under the finger, in reading order. Dragging back unpaints. Starting on a selected item deselects instead. A vertical swipe still scrolls, and holding the finger near the top or bottom edge scrolls the grid while painting. Tap toggles one item.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: In selection mode, a drag that starts mostly sideways (within about 40 degrees of horizontal) paints. So does a short hold (0.25s) followed by a drag in any direction, which is how you paint straight down a column. Anything steeper than 40 degrees without a hold scrolls, the same as any grid.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Painting covers the reading-order range from the first item touched to the one under the finger, like the system photo library. Dragging back shrinks the range and each item returns to what it was before the drag. Starting on a selected item deselects the range instead.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hold the finger in the top or bottom band (72pt by default) and the grid auto-scrolls while you paint. Speed grows linearly with depth into the band, up to 1200pt a second at the edge, and rows scrolled into view keep painting under a still finger.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A tap toggles one item. Outside selection mode taps reach your cell content (buttons, links), and with `longPressToSelect` a 0.45s hold turns selection mode on, selects that item and keeps painting. Pass `false` if your cells have their own context menu.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The gesture is a small UIKit recognizer the grid installs on its own scroll view. It decides between painting and scrolling within the first 8 points of movement, and the grid's scroll view (and any scroll view around it, such as a screen-level `ScrollView`) waits for that decision, so a paint never scrolls and a scroll never paints.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Columns are as many as fit at `minimumCellWidth`, so the grid adapts to rotation, iPad and split view. Selection is kept by ID across column changes. Items are hit-tested from the grid's geometry, not from cell frames, so painting works through rows a lazy grid has not built yet.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: When items disappear, their IDs drop out of `selection`, and a drag in progress ends. Turning `isSelecting` off keeps `selection`; clear it yourself if your design does.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Selected cells inset (`selectedScale`, 0.86) under a check badge in the bottom trailing corner. In selection mode unselected cells show an empty ring, so it is clear they can be picked. The badge scales with Dynamic Type up to 34pt, and never past a third of the cell.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a soft impact when a paint starts, a selection tick per item crossed (at most about 22 a second, so fast drags and auto-scroll do not buzz), and a selection tick on tap.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: each cell is one element with your content's label and the selected trait. In selection mode it is a button that toggles on double-tap. Every cell has a Select or Deselect action, and Select also turns selection mode on, so everything painting does is reachable without it. After a paint, the new count is announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Right-to-left layouts mirror the grid; painting follows the mirrored reading order.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the inset and the check badge change with a short fade instead of a spring. Auto-scroll still runs, since it is driven by the finger.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.disabled(true)` turns off painting, taps and the hold. `Style` sets spacing, corner radius, the selected inset, badge, check and ring colors, the auto-scroll band and speed.

title: Follow Scroll
description: A chat, log and live-feed scroll container that opens on the newest item and stays pinned to it while the reader is at the bottom, but never yanks them away once they scroll up to read; items that arrive below are counted into a floating Liquid Glass pill that jumps back to the latest, older items loaded at the top keep the visible row exactly where it was, and keyboard, rotation, growing rows and removals all hold the reader's place.

contents.content: Colors and metrics for `FollowScroll`. `.standard` is the house palette.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Opens on the newest item and, while the reader is within `followThreshold` (48pt) of the bottom, scrolls each new item into view with a short smooth scroll. Many items arriving in one update scroll once.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Once the reader scrolls up, new items never move the content. They are counted into a floating pill at the bottom, such as "3 new", with a red dot and a down arrow. Tapping it (or ⌘↓ on a hardware keyboard) jumps to the latest and clears the count; scrolling back down by hand clears it too. Items removed before they are seen drop out of the count.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: More than most of a screen above the latest with nothing new, the pill shows as a compact round jump button. Turn it off with `Style(showsJumpButton: false)`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `alwaysFollow` jumps to the bottom for chosen items even when scrolled up. Pass `\.isMine` so the reader's own sent message always comes into view.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `onReachTop` loads older items when the reader nears the top (within about three quarters of a screen). Prepend them to `items` before it returns: the rows on screen stay exactly where they are, including when the reader is resting on the very top edge. A small spinner floats at the top while it runs. It never runs twice at once, it runs again while a short list still reaches the top, and a call that adds nothing is not repeated until the reader scrolls away and back, so an exhausted history or a failed request never loops.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Stays pinned to the bottom when the container changes size while following: the keyboard (for a composer in `safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)`), rotation, or the last row growing as text streams into it. Scrolled up, the reader's place holds through all of these.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Replacing the whole array (another conversation, a new filter) starts again at the latest with the count cleared. Removing the newest items is not treated as a reset.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Only a scroll by the reader leaves the bottom: rows inserted above, lazy rows re-measuring and resizes never do. On iOS 18 and later a finger on the content also holds back any automatic scroll until the gesture ends.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `isFollowing` (optional binding) reflects whether the view is pinned, for a "Live" badge or a toolbar button; set it to `true` to jump to the latest.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `empty` is shown centered while there are no items. Rows are laid out in a `LazyVStack`, so long threads and logs stay cheap.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tracking: iOS 18 and later read `onScrollGeometryChange` and `onScrollPhaseChange`; iOS 17 measures the content in the scroll view's coordinate space. Both feed the same logic, and position is held through `scrollPosition(id:anchor:)` on the bottom-most row.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pill: Liquid Glass on iOS 26 (`glassEffect(.regular.interactive())`), a material with a soft shadow earlier, and a solid surface under Reduce Transparency.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the pill is a button read as its label ("3 new") with the hint "Jump to latest"; the scroll view offers a "Jump to latest" action while scrolled up; new items that arrive while scrolled up are announced once per burst with the final count.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Localization: `newItemLabel` gives the pill text and the announcement. The default is a localized "3 new" through `String(localized:)`; add plural variants in your String Catalog, or pass your own. The pill mirrors in right-to-left layouts.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: the pill and its dot scale, the label wraps to two lines at the largest sizes, and the hit area never drops below 44pt.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: jumps are instant instead of scrolling, and the pill fades rather than scaling in.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a light tap when the pill first appears with news, and a soft one when you jump. Nothing fires for each new item.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the pill's label, signal dot and ink, the Reduce Transparency surface, the spinner color, row spacing, horizontal and vertical padding, the follow threshold and whether the compact jump button shows.

title: Paged List
description: An async/await infinite-scroll list that prefetches the next page a few rows before the end, never runs two loads at once, drops duplicate ids across pages, ignores stale responses after a refresh or cancel, shows pulsing skeleton rows, a footer spinner, an inline "Couldn't load more" chip with a solid Retry block that keeps loaded rows, a quiet "You're all caught up" footer, and pull to refresh that replaces rows only on success.

contents.content: An infinitely scrolling list driven by an async page loader, with every pagination state handled. The simplest call is one line: `PagedList(load: api.page) { item in Row(item) }`, or for page-number APIs `PagedList(pageSize: 20) { page in try await api.fetch(page: page) } row: { item in Row(item) }`. To restart with new parameters (a search query, a filter), give the list `.id(query)`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `load` receives `nil` for the first page, then each page's `next` cursor, which can be a page number, an offset or an opaque token. Return `PagedListPage(items:next:)` with `next: nil` on the last page. For page-number APIs, `PagedList(pageSize:)` builds the cursor for you and ends the list at the first short or empty page.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The next page starts when the row `prefetchDistance` (5) rows from the end appears, or when the footer is on screen, so short pages keep loading until the screen fills. Only one load runs at a time; extra triggers are ignored.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Items whose `id` has already been seen are dropped, so an API that shifts under you (new items pushing old ones into the next page) never produces duplicate rows. Eight pages in a row that add nothing new end the list, to guard against a cursor that never ends.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Every load takes a generation number. A refresh, a retry or leaving the screen cancels the load in flight and starts a new generation, and any response from an older one is dropped, so a slow page can never overwrite fresher rows. A load cancelled by disappearing resumes when the list appears again. Throwing `CancellationError` or `URLError.cancelled` is never shown as an error.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: States: pulsing skeleton rows while the first page loads (pass `placeholder:` to render your own row redacted instead), a footer spinner while more loads, a full error view with a Try again block if the first page fails, an inline "Couldn't load more" chip with a solid Retry block that keeps every loaded row, and a quiet "You're all caught up" footer at the end (`endMessage: nil` hides it).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Empty: the built-in state is a short message. Pass `empty:` for your own view, for example `ContentUnavailableView("No receipts", systemImage: "doc.text")`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pull to refresh reloads from the first page and replaces the rows only when it succeeds. If it fails, the old rows stay and a "Couldn't refresh" chip with Retry appears above them.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `layout: .list` (default) is a plain `List`, so swipe actions and row modifiers work in your row. `layout: .plain` uses a `LazyVStack` in a `ScrollView` with `Style.rowSpacing` and `Style.contentPadding`. Appending pages never moves the scroll position in either.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: To restart with new parameters, such as a search query or filter, give the list `.id(query)`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Concurrency: state lives on the main actor; `load` is a `@Sendable` async closure that runs off it. Items must be `Identifiable & Sendable`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`PagedListStyle`): `text`, `secondaryText`, `field`, `error`, `retry`, `end`, `ink`, `rowSpacing`, `contentPadding`, `skeletonRows`. Skeleton and badge sizes scale with Dynamic Type, and the error chip stacks its Retry block under the message at large sizes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: "Loaded 20 more" is announced when a page appends, and each error is announced. The skeleton reads as a single "Loading" element, the spinner as "Loading more", and Retry is a button with a hint.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the skeleton stops pulsing, the spinner becomes three fading dots, and chips crossfade instead of scaling in. A light haptic plays on Retry; routine loads are silent.

title: Status Timeline
description: A vertical status timeline where the live step becomes a solid color block, connectors draw in as steps complete, nodes morph from number to check, the current node breathes, and any step expands to show its detail.

contents.content: Vertical timeline for order tracking, delivery, or verification flows.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The live step is the graphic idea: its content becomes a solid block (`style.current`, tangerine) with dark ink, and its node matches with a breathing ring. Completed nodes are sage blocks with a drawn check, pending nodes are quiet numbered rings, and a failed step turns into a signal block with an x.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Layout is nodes leading, content trailing: a 44pt column holds the 30pt node and the connector below it, which stretches to the row's own height, so long titles and expanded detail never break the line. Rows hug their content, so the timeline never stretches to fill a tall container.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Connectors are trimmed paths: when a step becomes `.complete`, its connector draws downward in the text color over 0.45s and the node morphs from number to check with a `.success` haptic. After a `.failed` step the connector turns dashed with an `.error` haptic, so the trail visibly stops.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tap any step with `detail` to expand it; one step is expanded at a time. `expandsCurrent` opens the current step on appearance and follows it as the live step moves on. Detail on a block reads in ink; detail on other steps sits on a small `style.surface` card.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`StatusTimeline.Style`): `current`, `complete`, `failed`, `ink`, `text`, `muted`, `surface`. `tint:` still overrides both the current and complete colors.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion replaces the breathing ring with a static halo and swaps the springs for short fades. Each step is a single VoiceOver element that reads its title, timestamp and status, and is a button only when it has detail.

title: Swipe Action Row
description: Wraps any row in a soft card with swipe actions drawn as solid color blocks. Tiles grow in as the row opens, the drag rubber-bands, a full swipe arms with a haptic and lets the edge block take the whole bar, and a shared binding keeps one row open at a time.

contents.content: Row with swipe-to-reveal actions that works in a plain `VStack` or `ScrollView`, not only in `List`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Rows are soft cards (`style.surface`, 26pt continuous radius) and actions are solid color blocks with dark ink, separated from the card and each other by `style.tileGap`. Pass light block colors as `tint`; the house defaults are sky, butter, sage, tangerine and lilac, with signal (`#FF5B3A`) reserved for the one destructive or primary action.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Drags are only claimed when they start horizontally, so the enclosing `ScrollView` keeps vertical scrolling. The card lifts off the tiles with a soft shadow as it opens, and the row clips sideways only so that shadow is never cut.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tiles grow in: the glyph scales from 55% to full size with the reveal and the label fades in over the last half, so a short peek never shows cropped text. Tiles dip to 94% when pressed. A full swipe (past 60% of the row width) lets the edge block take the whole bar, bounces its glyph, fires a rigid impact at the moment it arms, and runs that action on release. The first declared action sits at the screen edge, matching `.swipeActions`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pass the same `open:` binding to every row in a list (with a unique `id:` per row) and only one row can be open at a time. Set the binding to `nil` to close all rows, or to a row's id to reveal its trailing actions (leading when there are none).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Swiping toward an edge with no actions rubber-bands to a 40pt limit and springs back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`SwipeActionRow.Style`, also `SwipeActionRowStyle`): `surface`, `tileInk`, `cornerRadius`, `tileWidth`, `tileGap`. `background:` still overrides the card fill; set `cornerRadius` and `tileGap` to 0 for classic full-bleed list rows.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion keeps every state change but replaces the springs and the tile grow-in with short fades. All actions are exposed as VoiceOver custom actions on the row.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Need grouped activity with categorize, split and expanding detail? That is the Transaction Row screen in SwiftPieces Pro.

title: Task Row
description: A task card whose check draws itself while the card flashes into a solid color block, a priority label block, a swipe-right that completes with a strike-through then compacts the row, swipe-left snooze and delete blocks, and a long-press lift that reports reorder moves.

contents.content: Interactive task row for to-do lists, driven by a bound `Status`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Rows are soft cards (`style.surface`, 22pt radius). Priority shows as a small HIGH, MED or LOW label block (tangerine, butter, sky) with dark ink; due dates carry a clock glyph; a snoozed task gets a lilac Snoozed label and a lilac check.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Completion is a sequence, not a toggle: the card flashes into the solid `tint` block (sage by default) while the check draws in with a trimmed path and a `.success` haptic, the strike-through grows across the title, then the row settles back and compacts (smaller padding and type, due label and priority fold away). Setting `status` to `.completed` from outside runs the same sequence; rows that load already completed start settled. `.open` reverses it. Reduce Motion crossfades every step at once.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Swipe right to the 104pt detent to complete (or reopen a completed row). The complete block's glyph grows with the reveal, the drag rubber-bands past the detent, and a rigid impact marks the moment it arms. Swipe left reveals Snooze (lilac) and Delete (signal) blocks, only for the callbacks you pass. Blocks and the check dip when pressed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Long-press (0.35s) lifts the row with a soft impact, scale 1.03 and a shadow; drag it vertically and `onMove` receives the number of row slots moved on release (negative is up). The gesture is only installed when `onMove` is set.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.disabled(true)` dims the row to 50% and turns off the swipe and lift.

contents.content: `Style` (`TaskRow.Style`): `surface`, `text`, `muted`, `ink`, `complete`, `snooze`, `delete`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `cornerRadius`. `tint:` still overrides the complete color.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Stack rows with 8pt spacing on the ground. VoiceOver reads the row as one button with status, due date and priority, and exposes Complete/Reopen, Snooze, Delete and Move up/down as custom actions.

title: Attachment Tray
description: A horizontal attachment strip for composers, support forms and listings: an add tile opens the photo picker with the remaining limit, each pick lands as its own tile that loads with a live progress ring, downsamples off the main thread into a crisp thumbnail and settles in with a spring, failures turn into a retry tile, the remove badge cancels an in-flight load, duplicates and over-limit picks are caught, and the caller owns every attachment for upload.

contents.content: A strip of photo and video attachments with an add tile, per-item loading, retry, remove and a limit. The caller owns the attachments. Picks from the built-in add tile are appended for you; anything else (a camera capture, a paste, a drop, a draft restored from disk, your own picker) is added by appending an `Attachment` to the binding, and the tray runs the same loading pipeline for it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: You own the attachments through a `@Binding [AttachmentTray.Attachment]`. Picks from the add tile are appended for you; the tray writes load progress, the thumbnail and the payload back by id, and removes an attachment when its badge is tapped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Anything else goes through the same pipeline by appending an attachment: `Attachment(image:)` for a camera capture or paste, `Attachment(data:)` for a drop or a saved draft, `Attachment(fileURL:)` for a file, `Attachment(item:)` for your own `PhotosPicker`, and `Attachment { progress in ... }` for your own download. For drops, add `.dropDestination(for: Data.self) { items, _ in attachments += items.map { .init(data: $0) }; return true }`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Each tile goes loading, then loaded or failed. The ring spins until the source reports progress (an iCloud download, or your loader setting `totalUnitCount` and `completedUnitCount` on the `Progress` it is given), then fills. Failed tiles show a red Retry disc; tapping it, or calling `attachments[i].retry()`, loads again.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Thumbnails are cut with ImageIO on a background task at the largest tile size times the screen scale, with orientation applied. The full-size image is never decoded, so a 48 MP photo costs a few hundred kilobytes, not a hundred megabytes. A text size change never triggers a reload.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Picked images keep their original bytes in `data` (HEIC stays HEIC, nothing is transcoded). `jpegData(maxPixelSize:compressionQuality:)` gives an upload-ready JPEG, downsampled, with location and other metadata removed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Videos (with `matching: .videos` or `.any(of: [.images, .videos])`) are copied to the temporary directory, never loaded into memory. `fileURL` points at the copy, the tile shows a poster frame and a duration badge, and `duration` is set. Delete the copy after upload if you need the space sooner than the system does.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Removing a tile cancels its load, including the photo library transfer. A load that finishes after its tile was removed, or after a newer attempt started, is dropped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The picker only allows the remaining count. Photos already in the tray (matched by library identifier, also within one pick) are skipped and their tile pulses into view. Anything past the limit is left out with a warning haptic and one announcement. At the limit the add tile shows "6/6" and disables.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Set `uploadProgress` on an attachment to show your upload: the tile dims under a ring while below 1 and shows a check once it reaches 1.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Empty, the add tile is wide and shows the title with "Up to 6". With attachments it shrinks to a square with the count. New tiles spring in and the strip scrolls to them; removed tiles shrink away.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Loaded tiles call `onSelect` when tapped, for example to open a full-screen viewer. Every tile has a context menu with Remove (and Retry when failed).

contents.heading: notes

contents.heading: notes
