title: Link Preview
description: A rich card for any URL that holds its final size while a skeleton sweeps, then settles the page's image, title and host into place, fetched once with LinkPresentation, shared by every card showing the same link and cached so scrolling never refetches, falling back to a quiet card with the address when a page cannot be read, opening on tap and offering Copy Link and Share on long press.

contents.content: A rich preview card for a URL: the page's image, title and host, fetched once and cached. Tapping opens `url` through the environment's `openURL`, so an app that shows links in its own browser routes it with `.environment(\.openURL, OpenURLAction { url in … })` like any other link.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `LinkPreview(url:)` fetches the page with LinkPresentation and shows its image, title and host. Pass `metadata:` to show your own (previews, tests, links your server already unfurled) with no request.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Three states, one footprint. While loading, the card is a skeleton built from the real layout, so the large card keeps its exact size when the content arrives: the image settles in with a short fade and scale, the text fades in. A page that cannot be read (offline, timeout, unknown host, a page with nothing in it) becomes the quiet address card: a link glyph, the host and the address, still tappable.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.compact` is a row with a square thumbnail, for chats and lists. `.large` puts a 1.91 : 1 image on top, capped at 280pt tall so a wide card crops instead of growing. Both take the width they are offered. A failed large card shrinks to the compact address card.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: No image falls back to the site icon on a quiet tile, then to the host's first letter on a solid block picked from the host, so a site keeps its color. A tiny "image" is treated as an icon rather than stretched.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Links that are not `http` or `https` never make a request: email, phone and message links show the address card with their own glyph and a meta line such as "Email".

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Redirects show the final host. Titles are trimmed with runs of whitespace collapsed, at most two lines (three at accessibility sizes). Long addresses truncate in the middle.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: One cache for the whole app: at most 150 pages and about 48 MB of decoded images in an `NSCache`, emptied by the system under memory pressure. Cards showing the same URL share one fetch, a card that scrolls back into view starts from the cache with no skeleton, and a failure is remembered for 30 seconds so a failing link does not refetch on every scroll.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A card that disappears or changes its URL stops waiting at once; the fetch itself is cancelled when no card is waiting for it. A late result can never land on a card whose URL has changed. `timeout` (15 seconds) is enforced even while a connection is still being attempted.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Each fetch uses its own `LPMetadataProvider`, created, started and cancelled on the main actor. Images are decoded and downsampled with ImageIO off the main actor and never kept at full size.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Tap opens the link through the environment's `openURL`, so an app with its own browser routes it with `.environment(\.openURL, OpenURLAction { … })`. Long press shows Open Link, Copy Link and Share (with the title and image in the share sheet); copying plays a success haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: one element read as "Title, host" with the link trait, a Copy Link action, and "Loading preview" as its value while loading. Copying is announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: text scales, the thumbnail grows to 96pt, and at accessibility sizes the compact card stacks the text under the thumbnail at full width.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: no skeleton sweep, no press dip and no scale on reveal; content fades.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the card, skeleton, highlight, title, secondary and tile colors, the letter ink and the corner radius. `.disabled(true)` dims the card.

title: Photo Cropper
description: A crop step for profile photos, posts and listings that keeps the picked photo covering a frame of the chosen aspect at every zoom and offset, pinches around the fingers while it pans, rubber-bands past its limits and springs back with a red flash on the frame and a rigid tick at a zoom limit, morphs between circle, square, 4:5, 16:9 and the photo's own shape without losing the subject, turns a quarter at a time, fades in a rule-of-thirds grid under the finger, and renders the crop off the main thread at the original's full resolution together with its pixel rect and rotation for cropping again on a server.

contents.content: A crop step for a picked photo: the photo under a frame of the chosen aspect, with pinch, pan, rotate and aspect chips. The photo always covers the frame. It can't be zoomed out or dragged so far that an empty edge stays in the frame: past a limit it resists and springs back on release. The framing is stored relative to the photo (zoom relative to the smallest scale that fills the frame, and the photo point at the frame's centre), so rotating, switching aspect and size changes keep the same subject in frame. Choose renders the crop from the original, off the main actor, and hands you a `Crop`. A drag that starts on the photo pans it; it never scrolls an enclosing scroll view or pulls a sheet down. ``swift @State private var photo: UIImage   // keep it in state, never create it in `body` PhotoCropper(image: photo, aspect: .circle, onCancel: { dismiss() }) { crop in avatar = crop.image dismiss() } ``

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Put it after a `PhotosPicker` (or the camera) in a `.fullScreenCover`, a pushed screen or a sheet. Keep the photo in state, for example `@State private var photo: UIImage?`, never created in `body`: a new image starts the cropper over.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The photo always covers the frame. Zoom is relative to the smallest scale that fills the frame (1 to 5, less for very small photos so a crop never drops below 32 pixels), and the framing is stored as that zoom plus the photo point at the frame's centre. Rotating, switching aspect, rotating the device and resizing all keep the same subject in frame.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pinch zooms about the fingers while they pan, both at once. Past the edges of the photo, or past 1x and the maximum zoom, it follows with a scroll view's resistance and springs back on release, with a short coast from a flick. At a zoom limit the frame's edge and corner marks flash red for an instant with a rigid tick. Double-tap toggles between filling the frame and 2.5x about the tapped point.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A rule-of-thirds grid fades in while a finger is down and out half a second after the last one lifts. The zoom level shows above the frame while pinching.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The aspect chips default to circle, square, 4:5, 16:9 and the photo's own shape; pass your own list (`[.square, .portrait, .ratio(3, 2)]`), retitle one with `.titled("Post")`, or pass a single aspect (or none) for a fixed frame. The selected chip's picture turns solid red. `.circle` shows a round frame but the crop is square: clip it when you draw it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Rotate turns the photo a quarter to the left each tap; quick taps keep turning the same way. Mid-turn the photo grows just enough that the frame's corners never leave it. `.original` turns with the photo.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Choose renders from the original, off the main actor, in the photo's own color space (Display P3 stays P3), upright, at up to `maxOutputDimension` (4096) on the longer side and never scaled up. `onCrop` gets a `Crop` with the `image`, the `rect` in pixels of the upright original and `quarterTurns` (to the left, applied after the rect), so a server can repeat the crop on the original, plus the `framing`. Choose spins until your `onCrop` returns, so you can await an upload there, then shows a check. If the cropper goes away mid-render the render is dropped; an `onCrop` that has started is never cut off.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `framing:` binds the aspect, zoom, centre and rotation instead of `aspect:`. Store `crop.framing` (it is `Codable`) and pass it back to reopen a crop where it was left, or drive the cropper from your own controls. Reset returns to the photo filling the starting aspect and is enabled only once something changed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: EXIF orientation is respected on screen and in the output. A photo that is much larger than the screen is shown from a copy cut once, off the main actor, so a 48 MP photo never decodes on the main thread; a quiet placeholder holds the frame meanwhile. A photo that can't be drawn shows "Couldn't open this photo" in the frame and Choose turns neutral. A failed render shows a short notice with an error haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A drag on the photo pans it: it never scrolls an enclosing scroll view or pulls a sheet down, because those pans wait for the cropper's own. Pinch and pan come from UIKit's recognizers, which report the fingers' moving centre.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a selection tick when the aspect changes, a light impact on rotate, a rigid tick at a zoom limit or an edge, a soft tick on Reset, success when the crop is delivered, an error if rendering fails.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the photo is one adjustable element, "Crop area", with a value such as "2.5×, 4:5, Rotated left 90°". Swipe up and down to zoom, and use the Move up, down, left and right actions (a fifth of the frame each), Rotate left and Reset. Aspect chips are buttons with the selected trait ("4 to 5"), and rotations, resets and the finished crop are announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hardware keyboard: the arrow keys move and + and - zoom when the photo is focused, Return chooses, Escape cancels and Command-R rotates.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the photo settles with a short ease instead of springs, rotation and the grid change without animating.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: chips and buttons scale (chips stop at the second accessibility size so the photo keeps its room). When the buttons no longer fit on one line, Choose moves to its own full-width row, and at the largest sizes Cancel does too. Right to left mirrors the toolbar; the photo is never mirrored.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the toolbar ground, the photo's well (dark in both appearances so the photo, scrim and frame read the same), the scrim, the frame's edge, the red accent and the ink on it, the chip and button fills, labels, the well's corner radius (`0` runs the photo edge to edge) and the frame inset. `Messages` replaces any of the copy, such as `choose: "Use photo"`.

contents.content: Parameter

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Description

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `image`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The photo to crop, at full size, such as one loaded from a `PhotosPicker` item. Its orientation is respected. An on-screen copy is cut from it once, off the main actor; the crop is always rendered from this original. Keep it in state rather than creating it in `body`, or every update starts over.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `aspect`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The frame to start with. Defaults to `.square`.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `framing`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Bound framing, instead of `aspect`: the aspect, zoom, centre and rotation, updated as people adjust them. Set it to reopen a crop where it was left (`crop.framing` from an earlier result) or to drive the cropper from your own controls. While a finger is down it can briefly sit past the limits (the rubber band); it settles inside them on release.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The aspect chips under the photo, in order. Defaults to circle, square, 4:5, 16:9 and the photo's own shape. One aspect, or none, hides the chips for a fixed frame. An aspect that isn't listed is added at the front.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `maxOutputDimension`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: The longest side of the rendered crop, in pixels. Defaults to 4096. Larger crops are scaled down to it; smaller ones keep the original's pixels and are never scaled up.

contents.heading: parameters

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: `style`

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Colors, the photo's well and the frame inset. Defaults to the SwiftPieces house palette, adapting to light and dark, with red for Choose, the selected aspect and the limit flash.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Shows a Cancel button (and Escape on a hardware keyboard) that calls this. `nil` hides it.

contents.heading: parameters
contents.content: Called on the main actor with the rendered `Crop` when Choose is tapped (or Return is pressed). Choose keeps spinning until this returns, so you can await an upload here.

title: Photo Viewer
description: A full-screen photo surface with anchor-correct pinch zoom, momentum panning that decelerates into the bounds, double-tap zoom about the tap, paging between images, and pinch-out or drag-down to dismiss with a fading scrim. A close button and a page counter that turns into a live zoom readout float above, and a single tap hides them.

contents.content: Photos-style viewer: page horizontally at rest, zoom and pan a page, pinch past the minimum or drag vertically to dismiss.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Zoom is anchored to the pinch start and to a double tap, so the content under the fingers stays put. Past `maxScale` the pinch rubber-bands with a rigid tick; releasing springs back. Returning to `minScale` plays a soft tick.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A released pan coasts to `predictedEndTranslation`, clamped to the scaled bounds, with a duration that scales with the distance, so a flick decelerates into the edge instead of stopping dead.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: At rest a page ignores horizontal drags so the paging `ScrollView` handles them; vertical drags and any drag during a pinch belong to the dismiss. Paging is disabled while zoomed or dismissing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Two dismiss paths: drag vertically past 140 pt (or flick past a projected 280 pt) and the page flies off along the release direction; pinch below 80% of `minScale` and release. Both fade the scrim with progress and call `onDismiss` when the animation is logically complete.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion shortens every settle to 0.2 s. VoiceOver gets Zoom in, Reset zoom, and the escape gesture dismisses.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: **v2:** floating chrome. A 44 pt close button (shown when `onDismiss` is set) fades the viewer out and calls `onDismiss`; a counter reads "2 / 3" at rest and turns into a light zoom readout ("2.5×") while zoomed. A single tap hides or shows the chrome, and the chrome fades as a dismiss drag progresses.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `style:` (`PhotoViewer.Style`) sets `scrim` (near-black #121212), `chromeFill`, `chromeInk`, `zoomFill`, `zoomInk`, `showsCloseButton`, and `showsCounter`. `.bare` draws photos only.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The example pages through flat color prints; a dismiss collapses the viewer and the example presents it again, so the preview only ever shows the viewer.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a full gallery screen, see the Pro Gallery screen (`depth-gallery`).

title: Story Strip
description: A Stories-style segment strip with a built-in clock that advances segments on a duration, a long-press hold that freezes the strip and shows a paused badge, tap zones for back and forward that answer with a chevron, and a manual progress mode when you own the timing.

contents.content: Segment strip plus the gesture surface of a story player. Pass `duration` to let it run itself, or leave it nil and drive `progress`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: With `duration` set the strip runs itself: a `TimelineView(.animation)` draws the fill and a task sleeps for the rest of the segment, then advances `current`. Pausing (a hold, or `isPaused`) records the pause time and shifts the segment start on resume, so the fill continues exactly where it stopped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Without `duration` the strip is stateless like before: you own `current` and `progress`, and steps animate with a short linear curve so 30 Hz updates read as continuous.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Holding anywhere on the surface for 200 ms freezes and dims the strip with a soft tick; releasing resumes. A shorter touch is a tap: the left 30% goes back (restarting the first segment) and the rest advances. Segment changes snap with `.snappy` and a `.selection` tick.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `fillsContainer` stretches the invisible surface over the whole story with the bars pinned to the top; set it to false to use only the bar row.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `onFinish` fires once when the last segment completes. VoiceOver reads "3 of 5", swipes up or down move between segments, and a custom action pauses or resumes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: **v2:** holding shows a "Paused" badge under the trailing end of the bars, and a tap that moves back or forward flashes a chevron in that zone. Bars are 4 pt by default.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `style:` (`StoryStrip.Style`) sets `barHeight`, `spacing`, `trackOpacity`, `inset`, `showsPausedBadge`, `showsTapHints`, and `ink` (the glyph color on `tint`). `.minimal` restores the version 1 look.

title: Drag to Dismiss
description: A modifier that lets a photo, card, or sheet follow a two-axis drag, rounds and shrinks it with progress over a styled scrim, reports its phase so the UI can say "release to close", then springs back or flies off along the drag vector past a distance or velocity threshold.

contents.content: Photos-style dismiss: drag in any direction, the view rounds and shrinks as it travels, the scrim thins, and a far enough drag or a fast flick sends it off screen along the direction it was moving.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Apply it to the full-size root of a sheet or full-screen cover, or to a card wrapped in `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)`, so the scrim covers the screen while only the content moves.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Commit happens past `threshold` points of travel or when `predictedEndTranslation` projects past twice that. The fly-off follows the release direction, travels far enough to clear the container, and runs faster for faster flicks. `onDismiss` fires when the fly-off is logically complete.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Scroll cooperation: a scroll view inside the content keeps priority until it is at its top. On iOS 18 the modifier watches the scroll view with `onScrollGeometryChange`; on iOS 17 feed it `scrollOffset` yourself. Upward drags at the top go to the scroll view, and the scroll view is disabled for the duration of a captured drag so it cannot bounce underneath.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Bind `progress` and scale your presenter from 0.94 toward 1 with it for sheet-like depth.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Phases run idle, dragging, armed (a rigid tick at the threshold), returning, committing. VoiceOver's escape gesture commits a downward dismiss. Reduce Motion keeps the scale at 1 and shortens the springs.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `style:` sets the scrim (`#141414` at 0.5 by default, `.clear` for none) and the shrink at full progress. `phase:` binds the current phase so the UI can switch a "Drag to close" hint to "Release to close" when armed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The `#Preview` is the single card the modifier moves: a butter boarding pass, with the modifier's own scrim behind it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a full gallery built around this gesture, see the Pro Gallery screen.

title: Floating Dock
description: A floating dock on a solid surface where the selected item becomes a color block with its label, a drag across the dock lifts each item under the finger with a name bubble and commits on release, badges count in a signal pill, and the whole dock tucks away on scroll.

contents.content: Floating bottom dock of 4–5 icon items with a solid block selection and a scrub-to-pick gesture.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The dock is a solid surface capsule with two soft shadows. The selected item becomes a color block (butter by default, or `tint`) with an ink icon and label; the others compact to icon-only 48 pt targets. The block moves between items with `matchedGeometryEffect` and the selected symbol bounces once.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Touch and drag across the dock to pick: the item under the finger lifts 5 pt, scales to 114%, and shows its name in a bubble above the dock, with a `.selection` tick per item. Release commits with a soft impact. A touch that doesn't travel presses the item (92%) and selects it on release. The block itself never stretches toward the finger.

contents.heading: notes

title: Index Scrubber
description: An A to Z section index for long lists in any scroll view: touch or drag the trailing rail to jump to the section under your finger with a selection tick per new section, a large letter block that follows the finger and rolls in the direction of travel, letters without a section dimmed or hidden, a dotted collapse when the rail is too short for every title, one adjustable VoiceOver element and type-to-jump on a hardware keyboard.

contents.content: A section index rail for long sectioned lists (contacts, glossaries, countries, recipes) that works with `ScrollView`, `LazyVStack` and `List` on iOS 17 and later. Touch down or drag along the rail to jump to the section under the finger. Most apps use the `.indexScrubber(_:proxy:)` modifier on a scroll view inside a `ScrollViewReader`; use the view itself when you scroll some other way, and place it on the trailing edge yourself.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.indexScrubber(titles, proxy: proxy)` on a `ScrollView` or `List` inside a `ScrollViewReader` is the whole setup. Give each section an id equal to its title (`ForEach(sections, id: \.title) { Section { … } }`). Jumps scroll without animation, the section's top at `anchor` (`.top` by default), the way the system index does.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The modifier insets the scroll view's content by the rail's width (44pt at the default text size), so rows lay out beside the rail instead of under it. With no reachable sections the rail takes no space and no touches.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Use `IndexScrubber(titles, selection: $current) { title in … }` when you scroll some other way; place it on the trailing edge yourself. `onSelect` fires once on touch down, then only when the finger reaches a new section, plus on VoiceOver and keyboard moves.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `index: .sections` shows your titles as they are. `.alphabet` shows the current locale's index letters (A to Z and # in English, from `UILocalizedIndexedCollation`) and matches each section by its whole title, then its first character, then its first character without accents; titles starting with a digit or symbol fall under #. `.custom([...])` takes your own entries.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Entries without a section are dimmed by default and a touch on one lands on the nearest section after it (or before it at the end). `missing: .hidden` leaves them out. The letter block and the haptic only change when the landing section changes.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: When the rail is too short for every entry (landscape, accessibility text sizes), it shows evenly spaced entries with a dot between each, like the system index. The finger still maps proportionally along the whole column, so a dot lands on the letters it stands for and the block shows the real one.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: While a finger is down the rail keeps its touch-down geometry, pinned on screen, so a jump that resizes the scroll view (a large title collapsing) never moves letters under the finger. It settles into its new place on release.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The letter block follows the finger with a spring and the letter rolls in the direction of travel. A `.selection` haptic plays on touch down and on each new section, never on dimmed entries or repeated positions.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The drag lives on the rail itself, outside the scrolling content, so it never competes with the scroll view's pan; the scroll view keeps scrolling everywhere else. A system-cancelled touch resets the rail cleanly.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: the rail is one adjustable element, "Section index", whose value is the current section. Swipe up or down to step through every section (including any the rail's entries do not reach); each step scrolls. Write `selection` from your own scroll tracking so it starts from the section on screen.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hardware keyboard: when the rail has focus, typing a letter jumps to it, arrow keys step between sections, and Home and End go to the first and last. The track shows while focused.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: letters, rows and the block scale up to the first accessibility size, then the rail collapses entries instead of growing; the block shows the section at display size while scrubbing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Right-to-left: the rail sits on the leading edge and the block opens to its inner side.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the block and the letter fade instead of scaling, rolling and springing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the letter, dimmed, track, block and ink colors. `.disabled(true)` dims the rail and ignores touches.

title: Stretch Header
description: A hero header for your own ScrollView and NavigationStack: a heavy display title and uppercase eyebrow over a solid block hero that stretches on overscroll, a title that shrinks toward the real navigation bar, a stat row that pins under the bar, and a solid bar that fades in.

contents.content: Hero header placed at the top of scroll content, paired with `.stretchHeaderBar(title:progress:style:)` on the scroll view.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Two parts: `StretchHeader` goes first inside your `ScrollView` content, and `.stretchHeaderBar(title:progress:style:)` goes on the `ScrollView` inside a `NavigationStack`. Share one `@State` progress between them. The modifier hides the system bar background, extends the scroll view under the bar, and draws its own solid bar in the style's `surface`, fading in with progress and gaining a soft shadow instead of a hairline.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The title is display type: heavy, tight, 40 pt and scaled with Dynamic Type, with an optional uppercase `eyebrow` above it. Overscroll stretches the hero upward and grows the title a touch; scrolling moves the hero at 70% speed and the title at 55%, shrinking it toward the bar, and the inline title fades in over the last 20% of the collapse. States: expanded, stretching, collapsing, collapsed.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style`: `.standard` puts ink on a solid block hero with no scrim; `.overImage` uses a white title over a soft scrim for photos. Both set `surface`, the house ground behind the pinned row and the bar. Copy a style and change one property to customize.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The `subtitle` row (stats, avatar, tabs) pins under the bar once the hero has scrolled past it and draws above the content that follows. Give it its own padding.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Progress comes from `onScrollGeometryChange` on iOS 18 (fed through the modifier) and from the header's own position in the `.scrollView` coordinate space on iOS 17. A soft haptic marks a deep pull.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion drops the title parallax and the hero lag but keeps the stretch and the collapse. The hero reads as one header element and is hidden from VoiceOver once collapsed, when the inline title takes over.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: A full settings screen built around a header like this ships in SwiftPieces Pro (`settings-screen`).

title: Spotlight Tour
description: A first-run feature tour for any screen: mark controls with .spotlightAnchor and .spotlightTour dims everything else through a cutout that springs from stop to stop as a red ring draws around it, sets a callout with step progress, Skip and a red Next below or above the target inside the safe area, lets taps through to the real control (which can also advance the tour), skips stops that aren't on screen, follows its target through scrolling, rotation and the keyboard, can show itself only once, and keeps VoiceOver, hardware keyboards and Reduce Motion in step.

contents.content: Walks people through the controls on a screen, one stop at a time: everything but the current stop is dimmed, a red ring draws around it, and a callout explains it with Skip and Next. Mark each control with `.spotlightAnchor("compose")`, then apply `.spotlightTour` once, high in the hierarchy: on the `NavigationStack` or `TabView`, so the scrim covers the bars too, or on a sheet's root. Anchors anywhere inside it are found, toolbar items included. Taps inside the cutout reach the real control. Steps whose anchor is not on screen are skipped; while none is on screen, the tour waits.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Two modifiers. `.spotlightAnchor("compose")` marks a control as a stop; `.spotlightTour(isPresented:steps:)` goes once on the container that holds them, ideally the `NavigationStack` or `TabView` so the scrim covers the bars too, or a sheet's root. Each `SpotlightTour.Step` names its anchor, a title and a message, and optionally an SF Symbol, the cutout's shape (`.automatic`, `.capsule`, `.circle`, `.rectangle(cornerRadius:)`) and its padding.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Put the anchor right on the control, before modifiers that widen its frame: `.spotlightAnchor("add")` then `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .trailing)`, not the other way round. Anchors report their frame in window coordinates through the environment, so toolbar items, safe area insets and other hosted content work. Use one id per stop.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: While a stop shows, everything else is dimmed and a 2 pt red ring draws itself around the cutout from the top. Next springs the cutout to the next stop, morphing between rounded rectangles, capsules and circles, and the callout travels with it while its text dips out and back so words never smear. `.automatic` picks a circle for small square targets, a capsule for short wide ones and a rounded rectangle for the rest, with corners running parallel to the target's.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The callout sits below its target when it fits, else above, else on the roomier side, always inside the safe area and the keyboard with 16 pt margins and at most 360 pt wide. Its nub points at the target's centre and hides when the callout had to overlap the target (very large text on a small screen).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Taps inside the cutout reach the real control, UIKit bar buttons included. With `advancesOnTargetTap` (the default) the tap also moves the tour on. Taps and drags on the scrim are absorbed with a small nudge of the callout and a light tap, so nothing underneath changes by accident. Swipe the callout toward the end of the line for Next, back toward its start to go back.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Steps whose anchor isn't on screen (a lazy row scrolled away, a view that isn't there yet) are skipped, and the count shows only the steps on screen. While no anchor is on screen the tour waits without dimming anything, then starts when one appears. The tour gives an anchor a moment before moving on, so toolbar items that report late and the frame changes of a rotation never make it jump. The cutout follows its target through scrolling, rotation, size changes and the keyboard.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `isPresented` works with `@AppStorage`: `@AppStorage("inbox.showTour") var showTour = true` shows it until it is finished or skipped. Or pass `showOnceKey: "inbox.tour.v1"` and the tour presents itself the first time the view appears and records completion in `UserDefaults`; `.spotlightTour(steps, showOnceKey:)` does the same without a binding. `SpotlightTour.resetShowOnce(_:)` brings it back, for a "Show tips again" setting.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `step:` takes an optional binding to the current step, to resume a tour or move it on when someone completes the thing you pointed at. The tour writes it as people move through and sets it back to 0 when it ends. `onFinish` reports `.completed` or `.skipped`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver: while the tour shows it is modal and the screen under it is hidden; focus moves to the callout, which reads "Step 2 of 4. Find it fast. Narrow the inbox by sender, date, attachments or unread." Skip and Next are buttons, Previous step is a custom action, the escape gesture skips, and each step change is announced.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Hardware keyboard: Return is Next or Done, Escape skips, and the arrow keys move along the steps in reading order. The tour never takes focus, so a text field keeps its keyboard.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Dynamic Type: the callout grows and flips above its target when it no longer fits below. At accessibility sizes Next and Skip stack full width, the symbol tile steps aside and the callout may use the full width. RTL mirrors the callout; the cutout stays on the physical control.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: the cutout and callout crossfade from stop to stop instead of travelling, the ring appears without drawing, and nothing scales.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a selection tick when a step changes, a soft impact when the tour ends, a light tap for a nudge. Nothing when the tour appears on its own.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: All copy goes through `String(localized:)` and can be replaced with `Messages` (Next, Done, Skip, Previous step and the "2 of 4" and "Step 2 of 4" formats). `Style` sets the scrim, the accent used for the ring, the current step and the Next capsule, its ink, the callout surface and text colors, the track, the corner radius, the ring width and the callout's widest size.

title: Toast
description: A single toast card with a solid color tile for its kind, a bold message with an optional detail line, a signal-colored action such as Undo, and a thin timer that pauses while touched; placed inside the safe area so it clears the Dynamic Island and rides above the keyboard.

contents.content: Presents one transient toast on the top or bottom edge.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Single instance by design. Presenting again while visible does nothing.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The toast is a solid card: ink in light mode, raised grey in dark mode. A color tile marks its kind (`.info` sky, `.success` sage, `.warning` butter, `.error` tangerine) and bounces on arrival with a matching haptic.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `detail` adds a quieter second line. The action is a signal-colored capsule that flashes a check, runs the handler, then dismisses.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The countdown is a `.task` on the toast and is cancelled the moment the toast leaves; touching the toast pauses it (the thin bar freezes and the card presses in) and releasing resumes from where it stopped. Swipe toward the edge to dismiss.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Placement reads the safe area of the view it is applied to: at the top it clears the Dynamic Island, at the bottom it rises with the keyboard. Apply the modifier to a view that does not ignore safe areas.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Colors live in `Toast.Appearance` (passed as `appearance:`), because `Toast.Style` already names the kind. The card is opaque, so it reads the same with Reduce Transparency.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The message and detail are posted as a VoiceOver announcement on appear; the action button is a real button with its own label.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For stacked, queued alerts with a notifications feed, see the Notifications screen (toast stack) in SwiftPieces Pro.

title: Expandable Text
description: A paragraph clamped to a line limit that measures whether it is really truncated, and only then fades the end of its last line into a trailing "more" link; tapping grows the block smoothly to its full height with no reflow, a "less" link collapses it, links stay tappable, and VoiceOver always reads the whole text.

contents.content: A "Read more" paragraph that shows `more` only when the text is actually truncated. SwiftUI cannot tell you whether a `Text` was truncated, so this measures three hidden copies at the real width: the full text, the text at `lineLimit` lines, and the text at one line fewer (which locates the last visible line). The copies re-measure on width, Dynamic Type and text changes. When the full height exceeds the limited height, the visible text is laid out in full and clipped to the limited height; the end of the last line fades out (a transparent mask, so it works over any background) and a `more` link sits in the faded space on the trailing edge. Expanding animates the clip to the full height, so lines never reflow or jump. Font and color come from the environment like `Text`: apply `.font(...)`, `.foregroundStyle(...)` and `.multilineTextAlignment(...)` to the piece. VoiceOver reads the full text in both states and gets "Show more" / "Show less" actions; the visual links are hidden from it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: SwiftUI has no API that reports truncation. The piece lays out three hidden copies at the paragraph's real width: the full text, the text at `lineLimit` lines, and the text at one line fewer. "More" appears only when the full height is taller than the clamped height, so a short text never shows it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The copies re-measure whenever the width, Dynamic Type size, font or text changes (`onGeometryChange` on iOS 18, a `GeometryReader` on iOS 17). They never read the expanded state, so there is no layout loop.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Until the first measurement lands, a plain `lineLimit` Text shows the same first lines, so first appearance does not jump.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Collapsed, the full text is clipped to the clamped height. The end of the last line fades to transparent through a mask and "more" sits in the faded space. The mask needs no background color, so it works over cards, images and materials. Set `Style.fade` to paint a gradient into a solid color instead.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Expanding animates the clip height to the full height. Lines are laid out once at full length, so nothing reflows or jumps. "Less" fades in under the text on the trailing edge; `showsLess: false` keeps the paragraph open.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Font, color and alignment come from the environment, like `Text`: `.font`, `.foregroundStyle`, `.multilineTextAlignment`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `AttributedString` keeps bold, italics and links. With `togglesOnTap`, tapping the body toggles too; a tap that opens a link does not toggle, and lines hidden below the fold have no hit area. Links open through your `openURL` environment action.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `isExpanded` lets you drive or observe the state, for example to keep one review open at a time.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: RTL: the fade and "more" sit on the trailing side, which is the left in right-to-left languages.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` sets the link color, link weight, fade width (scaled with Dynamic Type) and the optional solid fade color. `.disabled(true)` dims the links and stops toggling.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion: expanding and collapsing happen without animation.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver reads the full text in both states, with links in the rotor. "Show more" and "Show less" actions resize the paragraph for sighted VoiceOver users; the visual links are hidden from VoiceOver.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The "more" and "less" links draw at one line tall but have a hit area of at least 44 by 44 points.

title: Glass Text
description: Liquid Glass rendered on the actual glyph outlines of a string, one or several lines, with a specular Material fallback below iOS 26, a solid fill under Reduce Transparency and Dynamic Type scaling.

contents.content: Liquid Glass applied to text outlines via Core Text glyph paths. The glyph path is built once per string and font, then handed to `glassEffect(_:in:)` as a shape. Split the string with `\n` for a stacked display title; lines use tight display leading.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Glyph outlines come from Core Text (`CTFontCreatePathForGlyph`), so any `UIFont` works, including custom families. The path is built once per string and font, not on every layout pass.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: On iOS 26 the outline is passed to `glassEffect(_:in:)` as a shape. Below iOS 26 it is filled with `.ultraThinMaterial` and a hairline highlight; Reduce Transparency fills it with `.primary` instead.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The point size follows Dynamic Type via `@ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle)`, capped at 1.6x so a display word never leaves the screen. Pass `scalesWithDynamicType: false` to pin it.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Glass reads best over a backdrop with soft tonal variation; a flat color gives it nothing to refract.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Split the string with `\n` for a stacked display title. `Style.alignment` and `Style.leading` (0.86 of the font's line height by default) lay out the lines.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: States: Liquid Glass on iOS 26 with a soft lift shadow; below iOS 26 a layered fallback (Material, optional tint at `fallbackTintAmount`, a top light and a 1pt specular rim); under Reduce Transparency a solid `Style.solidFill` (`.primary` by default).

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver reads the lines as one static text.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a full purchase screen built around glass display type, see the Pro Purchase screen.

title: Picture Headline
description: A headline with living pictures stuck between its words like a hand-placed collage. Each word rises into place and each picture opens from a dot into a tilted sticker with a white rim, landing with a spring, a light tick and a flash of crop marks, then keeps drifting. Press a sticker to lift it. Use the built-in house-palette scenes (the sun is our red mascot), your own images or SF Symbols; it wraps like text at any width and Dynamic Type size.

contents.content: A headline with pictures stuck between its words like stickers, revealed in reading order. Write it as a list of segments: strings are words, pictures sit where you put them. `swift PictureHeadline(["Slow", .art(.sun), "mornings, long", .art(.waves), "walks and early", .art(.moon), "nights."]) .font(.system(size: 40, weight: .bold)) ` Pictures are sized from the font, so they follow Dynamic Type and every font you set. Each lands as a sticker: a white rim, a soft shadow and a small tilt that alternates along the headline, with crop marks flashing at its corners. Press and hold one to lift it. Text wraps word by word and a picture never breaks from the row it lands on.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Write the headline as a list: string literals are words and pictures go where you put them, for example `["Slow", .art(.sun), "mornings, long", .art(.waves), "walks."]`. A string can hold several words; each word rises on its own.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pictures land as stickers: a white rim, a soft shadow and a small resting tilt that alternates along the headline (`Style.tilt`, 4 degrees at most), so a line reads as placed by hand. As each one lands, four hairline crop marks flash at its corners, the crosses SwiftPieces draws on its artboards. `Style.tilt = 0` lays them flat, `Style.rim = 0` drops the rim and `Style.cropMarks = false` skips the marks.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Press and hold a sticker to lift it: it straightens, scales up and casts a deeper shadow above its neighbours, with a light tick, then springs back to its tilt when you let go. The press uses `onLongPressGesture(onPressingChanged:)` with a small tolerance, so scrolling over the headline still scrolls. `Style.lifts = false` turns it off.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Pictures are sized from the font: `Style.pictureHeight` is a fraction of the line height (0.82 by default) and each picture's `width` is in picture heights (2.4 is a wide frame, 1 a square). Set the font with `.font(...)` as usual and the pictures follow it, Dynamic Type included.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Words and pictures wrap like text with a private `Layout`, so the headline breaks across rows at any width and a picture never splits from the row it lands on. `alignment` sets each row's alignment.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The reveal runs in reading order. Each word slides up from behind its own baseline and each picture opens from a dot as tall as the frame into the full sticker on a spring, turning from flat to its tilt as it lands, its contents settling from a slight zoom. The stagger is sized from the number of items, so a short and a long headline both land in about `duration` (1.2 seconds by default). `delay` holds the start; change `trigger` to replay.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Three kinds of picture: `.art(_:)` draws one of five built-in scenes in the house palette (`.sun` is the red SwiftPieces mascot, bobbing and blinking over the sand; `.waves`, `.moon`, `.hills` and `.bloom`), so a headline looks finished before you have artwork; `.image(_:)` fills the frame with your own `Image`; `.symbol(_:fill:ink:)` sets an SF Symbol on a solid block.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: After landing, pictures keep moving: scenes drift (the sun bobs, the sea slides, stars twinkle), images pan slowly and symbols bob. Set `Style.drift = false` for still pictures. Drawing uses `Canvas` driven by a `TimelineView` at up to 30 frames a second.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `revealOnScroll` waits until the headline scrolls into view with `onScrollVisibilityChange` on iOS 18; on iOS 17 it reveals on appear.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Haptics: a light tick as each picture lands, in time with the spring, and another when you lift one. Pass `haptics: false` to stay silent.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: VoiceOver reads the headline as one header: the words in order, plus a picture's `label` where it sits, so `.art(.sun, label: "a sunrise")` is read and an unlabelled picture is skipped.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion drops the rise, the zoom, the tilt, the crop marks, the lift and the drift: words and pictures fade in together and pictures sit flat and still.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`.standard` is the house look): `pictureHeight`, `cornerRadius` (a fraction of the picture height; 0.5 makes a capsule), `tilt`, `rim`, `rimColor`, `cropMarks`, `lifts`, `drift`, `openDuration` and `openBounce`.

title: Text Reveal
description: Reveals a headline by characters, words or lines, rising from a baseline mask with a stagger sized to land in under a second, then wipes solid highlight blocks behind the phrases that matter.

contents.content: Staggered text reveal that wraps correctly at any width and Dynamic Type size. The stagger is derived from the unit count, so a 3-word title and a 60-character sentence both finish in about `duration`. Phrases listed in `highlights` get a solid block that wipes in behind them once they land, with the text flipping to dark ink under the block.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: The stagger is computed from the unit count: each unit animates for about half a second and the rest of `duration` is spread across the gaps, so long sentences do not crawl. Pass a larger `duration` for a slower reveal.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Words and characters are laid out by a private wrapping `Layout`, so the text breaks across rows like normal text and characters never split a word. `.lines` renders each `\n`-separated line as one wrapping `Text`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Splitting text into `Text` views loses kerning and ligatures between units; `.words` keeps them inside each word and is the best default for body-sized type.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `revealOnScroll` uses `onScrollVisibilityChange` on iOS 18; on iOS 17 it reveals on appear. Change `trigger` to replay.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: Reduce Motion drops the lift, blur and scale and crossfades all units together.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `.rise` now slides each unit up from behind its own baseline (a mask at the unit's bottom edge). Set `Style.masksRise = false` for the old 10pt float.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `highlights` takes whole-word phrases. A matched phrase is kept on one row; after its last unit lands, a `Style.highlight` block (butter by default) wipes in from the leading edge and an ink copy of the phrase is uncovered by the same wipe, so the color flips exactly under the block edge. Under Reduce Motion the block fades in instead.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: `Style` (`.standard` uses the house palette): `highlight`, `highlightInk`, `masksRise`, `blurRadius`, `highlightDuration`.

contents.heading: notes
contents.content: For a complete first-run flow with revealed headlines, see the Pro Onboarding screen.
